label: Origin relation: a real relation of a thing to another as to the principle of its being
term: is really related to as to the principle of its being, at a moment (Lean `OriginRelation.RelatedAt`)
definition: OriginRelation.RelatedAt v x g t: in history v, at moment t, x bears a real relation to g as to the principle of its being (esse). Explicitly identified PRIMITIVE relation; no axiom constrains it. Its bearer is the subject and its term is g. It is a real relation of x, not a relation of reason, and it may be non-mutual: g need bear no real relation back. It names no action of g at t: whether the term is acting at t is the separate open premise TermGives, and whether the term exists at t is the separate open premise TermCoexists. Ordinary meaning: a son is related to his father as to a principle of his being, and so is a moved thing to its mover while it is being moved. Distinguished from the tenseless EsseReceivedIn (DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN; receiver and received act, no term), from BeingGiving.GivesAt (definition 158301bc; the agent side, an occurrent giving), from the tenseless CausesIn (a cause of esse, no moment), and from co-presence (an existing thing need not be the term of any relation).
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred, introduced for the relational-receipt test (docs/notes/sustaining-vs-existential-inertia.md, section 6). It is modelled after ST I q.45 a.3 co. ('creatio in creatura non sit nisi relatio quaedam ad Creatorem, ut ad principium sui esse'), ad 1 (the creature's relation to God is real, God's to the creature of reason only) and ad 3 (the creature is the subject of the relation and prior to it in being), read in the pinned Leonine witness passage fb7bd7bb, and after ST I q.13 a.7 co. (passage 12d8ecc5): relations are of reason on both sides (including those between a being and a non-being, and of a thing to itself), real on both sides (including those consequent on action and passion, 'ut motivum et mobile, pater et filius'), or real in one extreme only, as knowledge to the knowable; the creature's relation to God is of the last kind. No claim attributes this definition to those passages, because the Lean relation is time-indexed and the texts do not index the creature's relation to moments. Structural properties: none built in (not functional in g, no persistence, no tie to presence or giving); irreflexivity and non-mutuality are separate typed predicates (Irreflexive, NonMutual), and the priority that q.45 a.3 ad 3 assigns to the relation on the side of its term is not typed. OPEN: whether the related term acts on the bearer at each moment the relation is borne (TermGives). The analyst's contrast of a mover-and-moved profile with a father-and-son profile uses two exemplars of the second class of q.13 a.7, while that article places this relation in the third class; the third-class (ordination or measure) reading is untyped. Would be sourced, in its tenseless content, by q.45 a.3 co. and ad 1 as already read; the gap is the indexing to moments.
